public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says OpenAI's newest models are expensive to run and that cost is a growing burden. Reporting based on The Information says OpenAI's cost of running its models quadrupled in 2025. It also says OpenAI's adjusted gross margin fell from 40% to 33%, below a 46% target, partly because the company had to buy expensive extra compute. That fits 'cost is a growing issue'. As context, OpenRouter measured that users moving to OpenAI's newest flagship, GPT-5.5, paid 49% to 92% more than with GPT-5.4. That figure is customer price, not OpenAI's own cost. The claim is vague and names no measure or model. The figures are unaudited press estimates covering all models, and per-token prices for older models kept falling.
limitations: The claim is vague; there is no threshold for 'costly'.
Inference figures are unaudited press estimates covering all models, not only the latest.
Rising total spending partly reflects higher usage, not only per-model cost.
The GPT-5.5 data measures customer price, not OpenAI's serving cost.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The latest models (other than GPT-5) are costly to run and cost is a growing issue.

statement.document_title: Breaking news, and how the end might begin

our_interpretation: Read as about OpenAI's latest models, given the paragraph's subject.
He names no measure and no period. As the most recent period public evidence could cover before the 2026-06-10 post, I use full-year 2025 (as reported in early 2026) through the post date.
Plain reading: serving OpenAI's newest models is expensive, and inference cost is becoming a bigger burden, for example rising inference spending or margin pressure.
OpenAI's inference costs are known only through press reports of internal documents, so the implied accounting basis is press estimates.
criteria.support_condition: Reports that OpenAI's inference (running) costs rose sharply or pressured its margins in 2025–mid-2026, or that recent flagship models cost more to serve or use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reports that OpenAI's inference costs fell or stayed flat relative to revenue, with margins improving and recent models cheaper to serve, in the period.
